characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness of 837.3 ± 15.3 HV for the 17Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 10 h (Table 3).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: load 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the value given by the average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: measure the Vickers hardness of the 17Al alloy after aging at 600 °C for 10 h

interfaces.interface_notes: Fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich phases form at the β-Mn interfaces in ultra-hard Fe-Mn-Al-Cu alloys; TEM of the analogous 17Al alloy aged at 575 °C for 6 h confirmed the β-Mn / FCC Cu-rich interface with FCC twins inside the Cu-rich particles. The FCC Cu-rich phase content between β-Mn interfaces decreases with increasing Al content.
interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-17Al-5Cu (at.%) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.
Hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Samples solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
This sample corresponds to the 17Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 10 h, followed by water quenching (aging range studied: 525–650 °C for 1, 3, 6 and 10 h).

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample repeatedly tested 5 times and values given by the average of 5 measurements
measurement_conditions.test_standard: Vickers hardness (HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester, 9.8 N load, 15 s dwell, average of 5 measurements)

phases_present.morphology: near-complete matrix (α almost completely transformed into β-Mn)
fine particles at the β-Mn interfaces

structures.overall_structure: In the 17Al alloy after aging at 600 °C for 10 h the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn (already within 1 h at ≥600 °C), leaving hardly any untransformed α; numerous fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates are distributed within/between the β-Mn.

unmapped_findings: The 17Al alloy aged at 600 °C for 10 h (837.3 ± 15.3 HV) is NOT the peak-hardness condition for the 17Al alloy; the 17Al peak hardness of 924.9 ± 25.8 HV was reached at 575 °C for 6 h.
Table 3 (17Al alloys) full 600 °C aging series: 862.7 ± 28.0 HV (1 h), 794.6 ± 58.1 HV (3 h), 840.4 ± 18.5 HV (6 h), 837.3 ± 15.3 HV (10 h); solution-treated 17Al baseline = 259.8 ± 1.5 HV.

SE-SEM images of the 17Al alloy (Fig. 8) are shown for 525/550/575 °C (1, 3, 6, 10 h) and for 600 °C-1 h, 600 °C-3 h, 625 °C-1 h, 650 °C-1 h; the specific 600 °C/10 h condition is not individually imaged.

EBSD characterization of the 17Al alloy was performed at 525 °C/10 h, 575 °C/6 h and 650 °C/10 h (Fig. 5), and TEM at 575 °C/6 h (Fig. 12); no EBSD/TEM data are reported specifically for the 17Al sample aged at 600 °C for 10 h.

The β-Mn SEM-EDS composition (Fig. 14: Mn 36.2, Al 16.3, Cu 2.6 at.%) and the nanoindentation intrinsic hardness values were measured only on the HARDEST sample of the 17Al alloy (575 °C/6 h), not on the 600 °C/10 h sample, so they are not assigned to this sample.
Fracture toughness KIC was measured only for the peak-hardness samples (15Al, 17Al, 19Al at their maximum hardness values), not for the 17Al sample aged at 600 °C for 10 h.
